changes: Added `v2/index.json`: every v2 feed with `Path`, `Schema`, `SchemaVersion`, `ContentHash` (SHA-256 of the content without per-run fields such as `LastCheck`/`UpdateHash`) and `ChangedAt`. Poll the index (it sends an ETag) and download a feed only when its `ContentHash` changed
`XProtectPlistConfigData`, `XProtectPayloads` and `BackgroundSecurityImprovements` keys are now written in sorted order (before: a different order on every run, so the files changed without new data)

Graded sources: every CVE fact names its source. Layer 1 Apple (advisory, CSAF JSON since 2026-09-14, Apple's own 'may have been exploited' sentence), layer 2 CISA KEV. SOFA's own pattern matches are no longer published: their text window reached neighbouring CVEs (off-by-one)

BREAKING: "exploited" (`ActivelyExploited`, `ActivelyExploitedCVEs`, `UpdateSummary.Stats.Exploited`, summary `ExploitedCVEs` and `Priority`) now comes from Apple and CISA KEV only. SOFA's heuristics no longer mark CVEs exploited (e.g. Safari's `sandbox_escape` matches)
BREAKING: per-CVE `Severity` removed (it was SOFA's own label, not a source). Apple's advisory severity is in `Advisory.Severity`
BREAKING (Safari): per-CVE objects use the same shape as the other platforms (`ActivelyExploited`, `InKEV`, `NISTURL`, `AppleExploitationNotes`) instead of passed-through fetch internals

Added top-level `Sources` (what each source key means, its layer, version) and `CVEDetails` (per CVE: `Exploited`, `ExploitedSources`, `Apple` text from the CSAF advisory and Apple's exploitation sentence, the `KEV` entry) to every v2 OS feed and Safari
Added `Advisory` per release: Apple's `ID` (APPLE-SA-<n>), `Number`, `URL`, `CSAF`, `Severity`, `Revision`, `Updated`, `AvailableFor`; page, JSON and ID share the advisory number
`AppleExploitationNotes` is now filled with Apple's sentence; tvOS/watchOS/visionOS now set `ActivelyExploited` per CVE; iOS/tvOS/watchOS/visionOS `UpdateSummary` counts match `ActivelyExploitedCVEs`
summary.json: `ExploitedCVEs[].Sources`
Added `v2/summary.json`: a small, facts-only summary of all v2 feeds for dashboards, bots, MDM tooling and agents (schema `summary.schema.json`)

Per platform, the majors Apple still patches (a release on either of the two most recent release dates), each with `Latest` (all builds, CVE count, exploited CVE IDs, `Priority`), the last 5 `Releases`, `DeviceSpecific`, the newest BSI and, for macOS 26+, `ProductKeys`
`Priority` in the summary: `critical` (actively exploited CVE, Apple or CISA KEV), `security` (CVEs, or details pending), `none`. The v2 feeds' `UpdateSummary.Priority` is unchanged
Additive: no existing feed changes; `bulletin_data.json` is unchanged
Additive (macOS v2): `Builds` on releases GDMF still lists: each build with the boards it serves (raw GDMF, not forward-accumulated like `SupportedDevices`; a board can appear under twin builds)

Additive (macOS v2): top-level `ProductKeys` (Software Update product keys, usable for the `AutoInstallProductKeys` preference, as an allowlist, or for compliance checks) keyed by the Mac's current major (26+; DDM-based Software Update, 15 and older out of scope): `Update` = keys for every release of that major GDMF still lists (every build; a deferred Mac is offered an older one; non-matching keys are ignored, write the whole list), `Upgrade` = opt-in keys for the next major (never together with `Update`), `BackgroundSecurityImprovement` = `_rsr` keys
Keys reflect observed, undocumented Apple behaviour; prefer the Mac's own RecommendedUpdates when available. `Build` is unchanged and can be a hardware-specific build: use `Builds`
Additive: pre-computed release cross-references on security releases and BSI entries
Added `PatchesRelease` on BSI entries — resolves the release the BSI sits on top of via PrerequisiteBuild match
Added `SupersededBy` on security releases and BSI entries — next release covering the same device scope, with DaysLater gap
Added `MergedInto` on device-specific releases — next universal release that absorbed the narrow hotfix
Consumers no longer need to derive the BSI→release / narrow→broader / superseded joins client-side
All three fields are optional and skip-if-none — no layout change for consumers that don't read them
BREAKING: v2 feeds introduce a top-level canonical `Devices` map — GDMF identifier -> {DeviceID, MarketingName}
BREAKING: Every `SupportedDevices` field is now a string[] of GDMF identifiers (was Vec<SupportedDevice> objects). Consumers resolve via the top-level Devices map
`SecurityReleases[].SupportedDevices` is now optional — absent means `inherit from parent Latest.SupportedDevices`. Saves ~66% on macos_data_feed.json size via suppression of redundant duplicates

BREAKING: All v2 feed field names normalized to PascalCase — `update_summary`->`UpdateSummary`, `supported_devices`->`SupportedDevices` inside BSI, `apple_slug`->`AppleSlug`, `macos_ipsw_*`->`MacOSIPSW*`, `cves`->`CVEs`, `entry_added_date`->`EntryAddedDate`, etc.
DMS consumer: `SignedVersions[].Build` backfilled from `bsi_history.ndjson` for historical macOS minor versions where live GDMF no longer carries the build string
v2 `InstallationApps` uses new PascalCase mirror structs (`InstallationAppsV2`, `UMAEntryV2`, `MacIPSWEntryV2`); v1 `InstallationApps` shape preserved exactly
Applied uniformly to macOS, iOS, visionOS, tvOS, watchOS feeds and `dms_consumers.json`. v1 feeds untouched.
Changed SupportedDevices from Vec<String> to Vec<SupportedDevice> with board_id, device_id, marketing_name
Removed BSIDeviceDetail and device_details field from BackgroundSecurityImprovements
BSI supported_devices now uses same SupportedDevice struct as release SupportedDevices
Added SchemaVersion field (CalVer) to all v2 feeds
Added schema_version to dms_consumers.json metadata
Added JSON Schema files (.schema.json) for all v2 feeds and DMS consumer feed
Added schema_changelog.json with version history
Added version_extra, device_scope, device_details to BackgroundSecurityImprovements
Added device_details resolution for all platforms in dms_consumers.json
Added content_hash to dms_consumers.json metadata
Enriched SecurityInfoContext with OS codename, BSI mention, days since previous
